# Starter: notification pipeline placement

This is a small, self-contained TypeScript project. It is **not** part of
the Berkeleytime monorepo -- it has its own `package.json` and
`tsconfig.json` and doesn't need anything else installed.

## Setup

```sh
npm install
npm test
```

`npm test` runs the test suite once (via vitest) and exits. Use
`npm run test:watch` if you'd like it to re-run on save while you work.

You should see all four tests fail against the code as given -- the
function they exercise is a stub that throws. That's the starting point,
not a setup problem.

## The scenario

`src/data.ts` holds fixtures modeling four consecutive runs of a periodic
enrollment puller:

- `SNAPSHOTS` -- an array of four runs. Each run is the *full* set of
  section snapshots (`{ sectionId, enrolledCount, capacity }`) fetched that
  tick, same as a real "fetch everything on a schedule" puller. Read the
  comments above `SNAPSHOTS` for what each section (`SEC-A` through
  `SEC-E`) is meant to exercise -- a basic open transition, staying open
  across a run (duplicate-notification risk), closing and genuinely
  reopening, a transition with zero subscribers, and a section that's
  never full to begin with.
- `SUBSCRIPTIONS` -- which emails are watching which section for an
  open-seat notification.

`src/mailer.ts` is a mock mailer (`createMockMailer`) standing in for a
real SMTP client. It never makes a network call; every "send" is recorded
in `callLog` so tests can assert exactly who got emailed and with what
content. Call `failNextSend()` on it to arm a one-time simulated SMTP
failure on the very next send, then it goes back to normal.

`src/notifications.ts` exports `processEnrollmentUpdate(previousSnapshot,
currentSnapshot, subscriptions, sendEmail)` -- given two consecutive runs'
snapshots, it should notify every subscriber of a section that just
gained an open seat (was full last run, has room this run), and return a
result per notification attempt (`sent` or `failed`). **It is currently a
stub that throws `"not implemented"`.** The JSDoc comment directly above
the function signature spells out the exact contract it must satisfy.

## The task

Implement `processEnrollmentUpdate` so that:

```sh
npm test
```

passes (all tests in `test/notifications.test.ts`). Do not edit the test
file or the fixtures in `src/data.ts` to make it pass -- write the
implementation. Use your Round 1 design as a starting point -- or revise
it now that you're working against the concrete types, fixtures, and mock
mailer rather than a whiteboard sketch.

The full test suite checks:

1. A section that transitions from full to open notifies its subscribers,
   and a section with no subscribers (or one that was never full to begin
   with) produces no notifications and no errors.
2. A section that *stays* open across a second consecutive run does **not**
   get re-notified -- a correct implementation compares each section's
   *current* snapshot against its *previous* one and only notifies on a
   genuine full-to-open transition, not merely "is open right now."
3. A section that closes and later genuinely reopens **does** get notified
   again -- this is a real, new transition, not a duplicate.
4. A failed send (simulated SMTP failure) is handled gracefully: it's
   reflected in the returned results, but it does not prevent other
   sections/subscribers in the same batch from being processed.

If your implementation changes the function's signature or the shape of
its dependencies (e.g. how per-section previous state is looked up),
that's fine -- just make sure the assertions above still hold in spirit,
and be ready to explain the change in the review.

## Logging AI prompts

If you use an AI tool (Claude, Copilot, ChatGPT, etc.) while working on
this, keep a running log of what you asked it -- a text file, a chat
export, whatever's convenient. You'll walk through it in the review.
